outcome: Revision history is directly navigable from the Experiment header
owner_impact: The Experiment header now shows exactly what you are viewing: a numbered revision or your Working copy. Opening it exposes retained history with All, Mine and AI filters, exact author/time/base provenance, and direct selection of old snapshots. New AI revisions become visible without replacing your current view or hiding your Working copy. If a Working copy already exists, inspecting another revision cannot overwrite it accidentally; starting from that revision requires an explicit Edit from this revision action.

next.text: #396 continues with #399 — the bounded integrated revision-workflow UX and regression verification pass. It will exercise the whole flow as one product experience and correct material friction found there. It has not started yet.

technical_evidence: Revision history reads the immutable public.experiment_revisions snapshots created by #397 and loads the exact selected artifact payload.
The revision control and Save Revision action live in the Experiment header; Account retains account, copy, collection and sharing concerns.
All/Mine/AI filtering uses retained revision authorship, with Mine defined as the currently signed-in account.
The experiments table is enabled in the Supabase Realtime publication; existing SELECT RLS remains the visibility authority and Realtime events are treated only as re-fetch signals.
A preserved Working copy locks inspected numbered revisions against accidental overwrite until the user explicitly chooses Edit from this revision.
Responsive and keyboard-accessible dialog/button semantics are covered by the #398 browser contract tests.
No CI/CD, deployment, retry, timeout, scheduling, connector-tool surface, or project-development workflow rule changed.

The responsive production smoke readiness probe is null-safe during Chrome's transient pre-documentElement navigation state; its retry count, cadence, readiness predicate, and completion gate are unchanged.
